unit: Unit 12: Everyday Life with Your Computer
title: Online Shopping and Banking
drDigitalIntro:
In Unit 10 you learned to spot safe websites. Now put that to work for real shopping and banking.

For banking:
1. Type your bank's address yourself — never click a link in an email or text.
2. Check for the padlock and 'https://' before you log in.
3. If your bank offers two-step verification, turn it on.
4. When you finish, click Log Out — do not just close the tab.
5. Avoid banking on public WiFi, like in a coffee shop or airport.

For shopping:
1. Look for the padlock before entering card details.
2. Pay by card or a payment service, never by bank transfer.
3. Keep the order confirmation email — it is your proof of purchase.
4. If a deal looks too good to be true, search the shop's name plus 'reviews' before you buy.

The golden rule: when in doubt, type the address yourself — never follow a link you did not ask for.
drDigitalSuccess: You know how to shop and bank safely online! The padlock, https, and typing the address yourself are your three best defenses.
drDigitalHint: The key checks are: type the address yourself, look for the padlock, and log out when done. You covered how to spot fake sites in Unit 10.
